sanskrit: na coktavantāv aśreyaḥ purastād api kiṃ cana na cāpy apakṛtaṃ kiṃ cid anayor lakṣyate tvayi
english: They have never before counselled what was harmful, nor is any wrongdoing by them toward you discernible.

sanskrit: tāv imau puruṣavyāghrāv anāgasi nṛpa tvayi na mantrayetāṃ tvac chreyaḥ kathaṃ satyaparākramau
english: How could these two tiger-like men, whose valour rests on truth, fail to counsel your welfare when you have done no wrong toward them, O king?

sanskrit: prajñāvantau naraśreṣṭhāv asmiṃl loke narādhipa tvannimittam ato nemau kiṃ cij jihmaṃ vadiṣyataḥ iti me naiṣṭhikī buddhir vartate kurunandana
english: These two foremost of men are wise in this world, O lord of men; for your sake they will speak nothing crooked — such is my settled conviction, O joy of the Kurus.

sanskrit: na cārthahetor dharmajñau vakṣyataḥ pakṣasaṃśritam etad dhi paramaṃ śreyo menāte tava bhārata
english: Those two who know righteousness will not speak in favour of any party out of self-interest; this they regard as your supreme good, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: duryodhanaprabhṛtayaḥ putrā rājan yathā tava tathaiva pāṇḍaveyās te putrā rājan na saṃśayaḥ
english: O king, just as Duryodhana and the rest are your sons, so too are the sons of Pāṇḍu your sons — of this there is no doubt.

sanskrit: teṣu ced ahitaṃ kiṃ cin mantrayeyur abuddhitaḥ mantriṇas te na te śreyaḥ prapaśyanti viśeṣataḥ
english: If your counsellors were to advise anything harmful toward them out of foolishness, those advisors do not truly perceive what is good for you.

sanskrit: atha te hṛdaye rājan viśeṣas teṣu vartate antarasthaṃ vivṛṇvānāḥ śreyaḥ kuryur na te dhruvam
english: And if in your heart, O king, there lurks some distinction between them, those who reveal that inner bias will certainly not serve your welfare.

sanskrit: etadartham imau rājan mahātmānau mahādyutī nocatur vivṛtaṃ kiṃ cin na hy eṣa tava niścayaḥ
english: It is for this reason, O king, that those two great-souled and radiant ones have said nothing openly — for that is not yet your settled resolve.

sanskrit: yac cāpy aśakyatāṃ teṣām āhatuḥ puruṣarṣabhau tat tathā puruṣavyāghra tava tad bhadram astu te
english: And what those two bulls among men have declared to be unachievable against the Pāṇḍavas — so it truly is, O tiger among men; may good come to you.

sanskrit: kathaṃ hi pāṇḍavaḥ śrīmān savyasācī paraṃtapaḥ śakyo vijetuṃ saṃgrāme rājan maghavatā api
english: For how could the glorious Pāṇḍava Savyasācī, the scorcher of foes, be conquered in battle, O king — not even by Indra himself?

sanskrit: bhīmaseno mahābāhur nāgāyutabalo mahān kathaṃ hi yudhi śakyeta vijetum amarair api
english: How could the mighty long-armed Bhīmasena, whose strength equals ten thousand elephants, be defeated in battle even by the immortal gods?

sanskrit: tathaiva kṛtinau yuddhe yamau yamasutāv iva kathaṃ viṣahituṃ śakyau raṇe jīvitum icchatā
english: And likewise, those two accomplished twins, like sons of Yama himself in battle — how could anyone wishing to live endure them on the battlefield?

sanskrit: yasmin dhṛtir anukrośaḥ kṣamā satyaṃ parākramaḥ nityāni pāṇḍavaśreṣṭhe sa jīyeta kathaṃ raṇe
english: He in whom steadfastness, compassion, forbearance, truth, and valour are ever-present — the foremost of the Pāṇḍavas — how could he be defeated in battle?

sanskrit: yeṣāṃ pakṣadharo rāmo yeṣāṃ mantrī janārdanaḥ kiṃ nu tair ajitaṃ saṃkhye yeṣāṃ pakṣe ca sātyakiḥ
english: Rāma champions their cause, Janārdana is their counsellor, and Sātyaki stands on their side — what could be unconquerable in battle for them?

sanskrit: drupadaḥ śvaśuro yeṣāṃ yeṣāṃ śyālāś ca pārṣatāḥ dhṛṣṭadyumnamukhā vīrā bhrātaro drupadātmajāḥ
english: Drupada is their father-in-law, and their brothers-in-law are the Pārṣatas — the heroic sons of Drupada led by Dhṛṣṭadyumna.

sanskrit: so 'śakyatāṃ ca vijñāya teṣām agreṇa bhārata dāyādyatāṃ ca dharmeṇa samyak teṣu samācara
english: Having understood their invincibility above all else, O Bhārata, and recognising their right of inheritance by law, conduct yourself rightly toward them.

sanskrit: idaṃ nirdigdham ayaśaḥ purocanakṛtaṃ mahat teṣām anugraheṇādya rājan prakṣālayātmanaḥ
english: This great and indelible disgrace wrought by Purocana — wash yourself of it today, O king, by showing them favour.

sanskrit: drupado 'pi mahān rājā kṛtavairaś ca naḥ purā tasya saṃgrahaṇaṃ rājan svapakṣasya vivardhanam
english: Drupada too is a great king, and one who was formerly our enemy; winning him over, O king, is the strengthening of your own side.

sanskrit: balavantaś ca dāśārhā bahavaś ca viśāṃ pate yataḥ kṛṣṇas tatas te syur yataḥ kṛṣṇas tato jayaḥ
english: The Dāśārhas are powerful and numerous, O lord of the people; where Kṛṣṇa is, there they will be — and where Kṛṣṇa is, there is victory.

sanskrit: yac ca sāmnaiva śakyeta kāryaṃ sādhayituṃ nṛpa ko daivaśaptas tat kārtuṃ vigraheṇa samācaret
english: When a matter can be accomplished by conciliation alone, O king, who but one cursed by fate would pursue it through conflict instead?

sanskrit: śrutvā ca jīvataḥ pārthān paurajānapado janaḥ balavad darśane gṛdhnus teṣāṃ rājan kuru priyam
english: The townspeople and the country folk, having heard that the Pārthas live, yearn keenly to see them — O king, do what pleases them.

sanskrit: duryodhanaś ca karṇaś ca śakuniś cāpi saubalaḥ adharmayuktā duṣprajñā bālā maiṣāṃ vacaḥ kṛthāḥ
english: Duryodhana, Karṇa, and Śakuni the son of Subala are given to unrighteousness, evil-minded, and childish — do not follow their counsel.

sanskrit: uktam etan mayā rājan purā guṇavatas tava duryodhanāparādhena prajeyaṃ vinaśiṣyati
english: I have said this to you before, O king — by the transgression of Duryodhana this people will perish.

sanskrit: dhṛtarāṣṭra uvāca bhīṣmaḥ śāṃtanavo vidvān droṇaś ca bhagavān ṛṣiḥ hitaṃ paramakaṃ vākyaṃ tvaṃ ca satyaṃ bravīṣi mām
english: Dhṛtarāṣṭra said: The learned Bhīṣma son of Śaṃtanu, and the venerable sage Droṇa, and you yourself — all speak to me what is supremely beneficial and true.

sanskrit: yathaiva pāṇḍos te vīrāḥ kuntīputrā mahārathāḥ tathaiva dharmataḥ sarve mama putrā na saṃśayaḥ
english: Just as those heroic great warriors, the sons of Kuntī, are the sons of Pāṇḍu, so by right are they all my sons — of this there is no doubt.

sanskrit: yathaiva mama putrāṇām idaṃ rājyaṃ vidhīyate tathaiva pāṇḍuputrāṇām idaṃ rājyaṃ na saṃśayaḥ
english: Just as this kingdom is ordained for my sons, so too is this kingdom ordained for the sons of Pāṇḍu — of this there is no doubt.

sanskrit: kṣattar ānaya gacchaitān saha mātrā susatkṛtān tayā ca devarūpiṇyā kṛṣṇayā saha bhārata
english: Go, Kṣattṛ, bring them here, well honoured, along with their mother and together with that goddess-like Kṛṣṇā, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: diṣṭyā jīvanti te pārthā diṣṭyā jīvati sā pṛthā diṣṭyā drupadakanyāṃ ca labdhavanto mahārathāḥ
english: By good fortune the Pārthas live; by good fortune Pṛthā lives; by good fortune those great warriors have won the daughter of Drupada.

sanskrit: diṣṭyā vardhāmahe sarve diṣṭyā śāntaḥ purocanaḥ diṣṭyā mama paraṃ duḥkham apanītaṃ mahādyute
english: By good fortune we all prosper; by good fortune Purocana has been quieted; by good fortune my great grief has been taken away, O greatly glorious one.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca tato jagāma viduro dhṛtarāṣṭrasya śāsanāt sakāśaṃ yajñasenasya pāṇḍavānāṃ ca bhārata
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Then Vidura, by the command of Dhṛtarāṣṭra, went to Yajñasena and to the Pāṇḍavas, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: tatra gatvā sa dharmajñaḥ sarvaśāstraviśāradaḥ drupadaṃ nyāyato rājan saṃyuktam upatasthivān
english: Having gone there, that knower of righteousness, learned in all the scriptures, attended upon Drupada in proper form, O king, joining him as was appropriate.

sanskrit: sa cāpi pratijagrāha dharmeṇa viduraṃ tataḥ cakratuś ca yathānyāyaṃ kuśalapraśnasaṃvidam
english: And Drupada too received Vidura in due form, and together they exchanged, as was fitting, the customary inquiries after one another's welfare.

sanskrit: dadarśa pāṇḍavāṃs tatra vāsudevaṃ ca bhārata snehāt pariṣvajya sa tān papracchānāmayaṃ tataḥ
english: He saw the Pāṇḍavas there and Vāsudeva as well, O Bhārata; embracing them with affection, he then inquired about their health.

sanskrit: taiś cāpy amitabuddhiḥ sa pūjito 'tha yathākramam vacanād dhṛtarāṣṭrasya snehayuktaṃ punaḥ punaḥ
english: And he of boundless intellect was duly honoured by them in proper order, repeatedly with affection, at the bidding of Dhṛtarāṣṭra.

sanskrit: papracchānāmayaṃ rājaṃs tatas tān pāṇḍunandanān pradadau cāpi ratnāni vividhāni vasūni ca
english: He inquired after the welfare of those sons of Pāṇḍu, O king, and also bestowed upon them various gems and riches.

sanskrit: pāṇḍavānāṃ ca kuntyāś ca draupadyāś ca viśāṃ pate drupadasya ca putrāṇāṃ yathā dattāni kauravaiḥ
english: For the Pāṇḍavas and Kuntī, for Draupadī, O lord of the people, and for the sons of Drupada, gifts were given as was given by the Kauravas.

sanskrit: provāca cāmitamatiḥ praśritaṃ vinayānvitaḥ drupadaṃ pāṇḍuputrāṇāṃ saṃnidhau keśavasya ca
english: And he of boundless wisdom spoke humbly and with courtesy to Drupada in the presence of the sons of Pāṇḍu and of Keśava.

sanskrit: rājañ śṛṇu sahāmātyaḥ saputraś ca vaco mama dhṛtarāṣṭraḥ saputras tvāṃ sahāmātyaḥ sabāndhavaḥ
english: O king, hear my words together with your ministers and sons — Dhṛtarāṣṭra together with his sons, ministers, and kinsmen...

sanskrit: abravīt kuśalaṃ rājan prīyamāṇaḥ punaḥ punaḥ prītimāṃs te dṛḍhaṃ cāpi saṃbandhena narādhipa
english: ...inquires after your welfare, O king, again and again with joy; and he is deeply gladdened by the alliance with you, O lord of men.

sanskrit: tathā bhīṣmaḥ śāṃtanavaḥ kauravaiḥ saha sarvaśaḥ kuśalaṃ tvāṃ mahāprājñaḥ sarvataḥ paripṛcchati
english: Likewise Bhīṣma son of Śaṃtanu, greatly wise, together with all the Kauravas, inquires after your welfare in every respect.

sanskrit: bhāradvājo maheṣvāso droṇaḥ priyasakhas tava samāśleṣam upetya tvāṃ kuśalaṃ paripṛcchati
english: Droṇa the son of Bharadvāja, the great archer and your dear friend, approaches you in a close embrace and inquires after your welfare.

sanskrit: dhṛtarāṣṭraś ca pāñcālya tvayā saṃbandham īyivān kṛtārthaṃ manyate ''tmānaṃ tathā sarve 'pi kauravāḥ
english: Dhṛtarāṣṭra, O Pāñcālya, considers himself fulfilled in having obtained alliance with you, and so do all the Kauravas.

sanskrit: na tathā rājyasaṃprāptis teṣāṃ prītikarī matā yathā saṃbandhakaṃ prāpya yajñasena tvayā saha
english: Their gaining a kingdom is not considered to bring them as much joy as obtaining this alliance with you, O Yajñasena.

sanskrit: etad viditvā tu bhavān prasthāpayatu pāṇḍavān draṣṭuṃ hi pāṇḍudāyādāṃs tvarante kuravo bhṛśam
english: Knowing this, may you dispatch the Pāṇḍavas; for the Kauravas are greatly eager to see the heirs of Pāṇḍu.

sanskrit: viproṣitā dīrghakālam ime cāpi nararṣabhāḥ utsukā nagaraṃ draṣṭuṃ bhaviṣyanti pṛthā tathā
english: These bulls among men have been away for a long time, and Pṛthā too will be eager to see the city.

sanskrit: kṛṣṇām api ca pāñcālīṃ sarvāḥ kuruvarastriyaḥ draṣṭukāmāḥ pratīkṣante puraṃ ca viṣayaṃ ca naḥ
english: And all the noble ladies of the Kurus are eagerly awaiting to see Kṛṣṇā the Pāñcālī, as well as our city and realm.

sanskrit: sa bhavān pāṇḍuputrāṇām ājñāpayatu māciram gamanaṃ sahadārāṇām etad āgamanaṃ mama
english: May you, without delay, instruct the sons of Pāṇḍu to depart together with their wives — this is the message I bring.

sanskrit: visṛṣṭeṣu tvayā rājan pāṇḍaveṣu mahātmasu tato 'haṃ preṣayiṣyāmi dhṛtarāṣṭrasya śīghragān āgamiṣyanti kaunteyāḥ kuntī ca saha kṛṣṇayā
english: When you have sent forth the great-souled Pāṇḍavas, O king, I shall then dispatch Dhṛtarāṣṭra's swift messengers; the sons of Kuntī will come, and Kuntī together with Kṛṣṇā.

sanskrit: drupada uvāca evam etan mahāprājña yathāttha vidurādya mām mamāpi paramo harṣaḥ saṃbandhe 'smin kṛte vibho
english: Drupada said: O greatly wise Vidura, it is even as you say to me today; I too feel supreme joy at this alliance having been made, O lord.

sanskrit: gamanaṃ cāpi yuktaṃ syād gṛham eṣāṃ mahātmanām na tu tāvan mayā yuktam etad vaktuṃ svayaṃ girā
english: And their going home would indeed be proper; yet it is not for me to say so myself in my own words just now.

sanskrit: yadā tu manyate vīraḥ kuntīputro yudhiṣṭhiraḥ bhīmasenārjunau caiva yamau ca puruṣarṣabhau
english: When the heroic Yudhiṣṭhira son of Kuntī thinks fit, and Bhīmasena and Arjuna, and the twins who are bulls among men,

sanskrit: rāmakṛṣṇau ca dharmajñau tadā gacchantu pāṇḍavāḥ etau hi puruṣavyāghrāv eṣāṃ priyahite ratau
english: and also Rāma and Kṛṣṇa who know righteousness — then let the Pāṇḍavas go; for these two tiger-like men are devoted to what is dear and beneficial to them.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca paravanto vayaṃ rājaṃs tvayi sarve sahānugāḥ yathā vakṣyasi naḥ prītyā kariṣyāmas tathā vayam
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: O king, we all along with our followers are subject to you; whatever you will say to us with affection, so shall we do.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca tato 'bravīd vāsudevo gamanaṃ mama rocate yathā vā manyate rājā drupadaḥ sarvadharmavit
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Then Vāsudeva said: Departure pleases me, or whatever King Drupada, the knower of all righteousness, may think.

sanskrit: drupada uvāca yathaiva manyate vīro dāśārhaḥ puruṣottamaḥ prāptakālaṃ mahābāhuḥ sā buddhir niścitā mama
english: Drupada said: Whatever the heroic Dāśārha, the best of men, the long-armed one, regards as timely — that judgment is my settled conviction.

sanskrit: yathaiva hi mahābhāgāḥ kaunteyā mama sāṃpratam tathaiva vāsudevasya pāṇḍuputrā na saṃśayaḥ
english: For just as the greatly blessed sons of Kuntī are now mine, so too are the sons of Pāṇḍu Vāsudeva's — of this there is no doubt.

sanskrit: na tad dhyāyati kaunteyo dharmaputro yudhiṣṭhiraḥ yad eṣāṃ puruṣavyāghraḥ śreyo dhyāyati keśavaḥ
english: The son of Kuntī, Yudhiṣṭhira born of Dharma, does not contemplate for them what Keśava the tiger among men contemplates for their good.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca tatas te samanujñātā drupadena mahātmanā pāṇḍavāś caiva kṛṣṇaś ca viduraś ca mahāmatiḥ
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Then, given leave by the great-souled Drupada, the Pāṇḍavas and Kṛṣṇa and the great-minded Vidura

sanskrit: ādāya draupadīṃ kṛṣṇāṃ kuntīṃ caiva yaśasvinīm savihāraṃ sukhaṃ jagmur nagaraṃ nāgasāhvayam
english: took Draupadī Kṛṣṇā and the illustrious Kuntī and journeyed in ease and comfort to the city named after the serpent — Hāstinapura.

sanskrit: śrutvā copasthitān vīrān dhṛtarāṣṭro 'pi kauravaḥ pratigrahāya pāṇḍūnāṃ preṣayām āsa kauravān
english: And Dhṛtarāṣṭra the Kaurava, hearing that the heroes were approaching, sent the Kauravas to receive the Pāṇḍavas.

sanskrit: vikarṇaṃ ca maheṣvāsaṃ citrasenaṃ ca bhārata droṇaṃ ca parameṣvāsaṃ gautamaṃ kṛpam eva ca
english: He sent Vikarṇa the great archer and Citrasena, O Bhārata, and Droṇa the supreme archer and Kṛpa the son of Gautama.

sanskrit: tais te parivṛtā vīrāḥ śobhamānā mahārathāḥ nagaraṃ hāstinapuraṃ śanaiḥ praviviśus tadā
english: Surrounded by them, those heroic and resplendent great warriors then slowly entered the city of Hāstinapura.

sanskrit: kautūhalena nagaraṃ dīryamāṇam ivābhavat yatra te puruṣavyāghrāḥ śokaduḥkhavināśanāḥ
english: The city seemed to burst with excitement as those tiger-like men — who dispel grief and sorrow — entered.

sanskrit: tata uccāvacā vācaḥ priyāḥ priyacikīrṣubhiḥ udīritā aśṛṇvaṃs te pāṇḍavā hṛdayaṃgamāḥ
english: Then the Pāṇḍavas, who touched the heart, heard high and low voices of welcome uttered by those wishing to show them affection.

sanskrit: ayaṃ sa puruṣavyāghraḥ punar āyāti dharmavit yo naḥ svān iva dāyādān dharmeṇa parirakṣati
english: "This tiger among men, the knower of righteousness, returns — he who protects us with righteousness as though we were his own heirs."

sanskrit: adya pāṇḍur mahārājo vanād iva vanapriyaḥ āgataḥ priyam asmākaṃ cikīrṣur nātra saṃśayaḥ
english: "Today great King Pāṇḍu has returned as though from the forest, he who loves the forest — come to do what is dear to us; of this there is no doubt."

sanskrit: kiṃ nu nādya kṛtaṃ tāvat sarveṣāṃ naḥ paraṃ priyam yan naḥ kuntīsutā vīrā bhartāraḥ punarāgatāḥ
english: "What has not been done today that is supremely dear to all of us — for the heroic sons of Kuntī, our lords, have returned?"

sanskrit: yadi dattaṃ yadi hutaṃ vidyate yadi nas tapaḥ tena tiṣṭhantu nagare pāṇḍavāḥ śaradāṃ śatam
english: "If we have given gifts, if we have offered oblations, if we have performed austerities — by that merit, may the Pāṇḍavas dwell in the city for a hundred autumns."

sanskrit: tatas te dhṛtarāṣṭrasya bhīṣmasya ca mahātmanaḥ anyeṣāṃ ca tadarhāṇāṃ cakruḥ pādābhivandanam
english: Then they paid reverence at the feet of Dhṛtarāṣṭra and the great-souled Bhīṣma and of the others who were worthy of such honour.

sanskrit: kṛtvā tu kuśalapraśnaṃ sarveṇa nagareṇa te samāviśanta veśmāni dhṛtarāṣṭrasya śāsanāt
english: Having exchanged greetings with the entire city, they entered their quarters by the command of Dhṛtarāṣṭra.

sanskrit: viśrāntās te mahātmānaḥ kaṃ cit kālaṃ mahābalāḥ āhūtā dhṛtarāṣṭreṇa rājñā śāṃtanavena ca
english: After resting for some time, those great-souled and mighty men were summoned by King Dhṛtarāṣṭra and by the son of Śaṃtanu.

sanskrit: dhṛtarāṣṭra uvāca bhrātṛbhiḥ saha kaunteya nibodhedaṃ vaco mama punar vo vigraho mā bhūt khāṇḍavaprastham āviśa
english: Dhṛtarāṣṭra said: O son of Kuntī, hear these words of mine together with your brothers — let there be no conflict between you again; enter Khāṇḍavaprastha.

sanskrit: na ca vo vasatas tatra kaś cic chaktaḥ prabādhitum saṃrakṣyamāṇān pārthena tridaśān iva vajriṇā ardhaṃ rājyasya saṃprāpya khāṇḍavaprastham āviśa
english: And no one will be able to trouble you while you dwell there, protected by Pārtha as the thirty gods are protected by the wielder of the thunderbolt; having obtained half the kingdom, enter Khāṇḍavaprastha.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca pratigṛhya tu tad vākyaṃ nṛpaṃ sarve praṇamya ca pratasthire tato ghoraṃ vanaṃ tan manujarṣabhāḥ ardhaṃ rājyasya saṃprāpya khāṇḍavaprastham āviśan
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Accepting that command and bowing to the king, those bulls among men departed thence toward that formidable forest, and having obtained half the kingdom, they entered Khāṇḍavaprastha.

sanskrit: tatas te pāṇḍavās tatra gatvā kṛṣṇapurogamāḥ maṇḍayāṃ cakrire tad vai puraṃ svargavad acyutāḥ
english: Then those Pāṇḍavas, unfailing, went there with Kṛṣṇa at their head and adorned that city, making it like heaven itself.

sanskrit: tataḥ puṇye śive deśe śāntiṃ kṛtvā mahārathāḥ nagaraṃ māpayām āsur dvaipāyanapurogamāḥ
english: Then those great warriors, in that holy and auspicious place, having performed the peace rite, laid out the city with Dvaipāyana at their head.

sanskrit: sāgarapratirūpābhiḥ parikhābhir alaṃkṛtam prākāreṇa ca saṃpannaṃ divam āvṛtya tiṣṭhatā
english: It was adorned with moats resembling the ocean, and furnished with a rampart that seemed to touch and cover the sky.

sanskrit: pāṇḍurābhraprakāśena himarāśinibhena ca śuśubhe tat puraśreṣṭhaṃ nāgair bhogavatī yathā
english: Gleaming like white clouds and like a mass of snow, that finest of cities shone with its serpents just as Bhogavatī does.

sanskrit: dvipakṣagaruḍaprakhyair dvārair ghorapradarśanaiḥ guptam abhracayaprakhyair gopurair mandaropamaiḥ
english: It was guarded by gateways fearsome in appearance, resembling Garuḍa with wings spread, and protected by gatehouse towers resembling piled clouds, like Mount Mandara.

sanskrit: vividhair atinirviddhaiḥ śastropetaiḥ susaṃvṛtaiḥ śaktibhiś cāvṛtaṃ tad dhi dvijihvair iva pannagaiḥ talpaiś cābhyāsikair yuktaṃ śuśubhe yodharakṣitam
english: Well guarded and covered with various weapons thrust in firmly, and encircled by spears like two-tongued serpents, furnished with regular watch-platforms, it shone with warriors as its guard.
